lines.text: Why is there a no-phones sign at every gas station?
Every gas station in the world has a sign telling you not to use your phone. It's been watching the wrong suspect.
What lights gasoline isn't in your hand. It's in your car seat.
The institute that tracks these fires has looked at nearly two hundred of them. Not one involved a phone. Not a single one.
In the lab, neither. A phone in a perfect cloud of gasoline vapor won't ignite it.
What shows up again and again is this: the driver gets back in the car while the tank is filling.
Clothes rub the seat, charges separate, and when you step out, your body is at several thousand volts.
Now the part almost nobody imagines. Inside the tank, nothing can burn. There's so much vapor and so little air, the mix is too rich.
What burns is the ring at the mouth, where vapor comes out and meets the air.
You reach for the nozzle, and before you touch it, the air breaks down. The spark jumps right at that ring.
Lighting that mix takes a quarter of a millijoule. The spark that makes you say ouch carries about four times that. On a dry day, twenty times more.
And you don't even need to get back in. Some fires happened before fueling started: the driver stepped out already charged, and the first thing they touched was the cap.
So the advice isn't don't get in the car. It's don't get in while it's filling. That stretch, and only that one, matters.
And since you charge up getting out, every time you step out, touch the metal of the door with your bare hand, away from the tank. The spark jumps where there's nothing to burn.
And if it catches anyway, your instinct will betray you. You'll want to yank the nozzle out. Don't. Leave it in, step away, and get them to cut the pump.
With the nozzle in, the flame stays at the mouth. Pull it out, and you spread it.
Same with gas cans: fill them on the ground, never in the truck bed. On plastic, the charge from the stream has nowhere to go.
It almost never happens. A couple hundred cases against billions of fill-ups. But staying outside for those two minutes costs nothing.
That sign should change its suspect.
